title: Odisha
name: Odisha
intro: Odisha has had 147 assembly seats since the 1976 order and has 147 today. The state was not divided and its assembly was not interrupted, so the constituencies drawn in 1976 were contested six times before the 2008 order replaced them. The redraw was heaviest in the tribal districts of the west and south, where the reservation of seats shifted with the boundaries.

map_caveats: The pre-2008 boundaries have been georectified. The source digitisation of the 1976-order map was displaced relative to the 2008-order map; the correction was fitted on the outer boundary of the state and raises the agreement between the two outlines from an intersection-over-union of 0.95 to 0.97.

Territory lineage is given on two footings, and each seat record states which applies to it. For 119 of the 147 pre-2008 seats the link is derived from the text of the 1976 and 2008 orders. For the remainder the successor shown is the one holding the largest share of the old seat's area, inferred from the boundaries alone.
Territory percentages are measured from the mapped boundaries in every case, and are areal shares, not shares of the electorate.
The reservation status of the post-2008 seats is taken from the constituency geometry, the source that carries it for this state.
footnotes: Odisha's assembly has had 147 elected seats since the 1976 order; the state was not reorganised between the two orders.
Reservation status reflects the category in force at the time of the relevant order, not any later reclassification.
